claim_being_audited: The Actor claims this release can be certified now based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 7% reversible rollout with monitoring, while the developer-support migration segment remains below target and exposed in the initial cohort.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy condition for a material model-card weakness: exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not sufficient when a named affected segment remains exposed.
Rollout percentage, rollback capability, and monitoring cannot substitute for disclosure duties or approved risk acceptance under the stated policy.
Public external guidance can contextualize governance but cannot override the internal policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide evidence that the affected developer-support migration use case is excluded from the initial rollout cohort.
Provide the reviewed risk-acceptance record authorizing exposure of the below-target segment before launch.
Provide the actual model-card disclosure or release documentation showing the material limitation is disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide evidence that the policy owner determined the limitation is not material, if that is the theory being used.
specific_concerns: The governing policy says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance.
The Actor's own summary says the below-target developer-support migration segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
No admissible evidence shows the affected use case is excluded from rollout.
No admissible evidence shows reviewed risk acceptance for continued exposure.
A rollback switch, dashboard, and small initial percentage do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The packet appears to rely on future or implied disclosure rather than evidence that required disclosure or acceptance is already in place.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently defensible on the available admissible record.
That reversible rollout mechanics and monitoring materially cure the disclosure problem while the affected segment remains exposed.
That public guidance on monitoring and model cards is sufficient support for this certification decision under the stated policy.
